title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

errors: The marginal qualifiers 'si det g = +1' / 'si det g = 1' on the identities Q=δ−a(c+d−b), S=δ−c(c+d−b) and R=(c+d)(c+d−b)−δ are unnecessary. These identities hold for arbitrary δ=det g (checked by expansion).
Equation labels are reused: (83) appears twice, and (84) is used both for δ^3=1 and for the case-2 system. The next page renumbers these as (85)–(87).
Minor ambiguity: the group is written SL(2,Ẑ)' ≅ ∏ SL(2,Z_ℓ)', yet determinants δ≠1 are allowed, i.e. GL(2) mod ±1. The computation itself is consistent with working in GL(2,Z_ℓ)/±1.
All matrix entries P, Q, R, S, the case split and the reduction to δ^3=1 check out algebraically.

ideas.what: Explicit solution of the 3-cycle relation g·ρ(g)·ρ^2(g)=1 for g in GL(2,Ẑ)/±1, prime by prime. The P-entry gives a dichotomy (a+b=0 or c+d−b=1/δ); in the generic case the remaining entries reduce to δ^3=1.
ideas.modern_name: Images of Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type cocycle (pentagon/hexagon, 3-cycle) relations in congruence/linear quotients of profinite mapping class groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara, Lochak–Schneps, Harbater–Schneps for GT relations; the explicit PSL(2,Ẑ) computation seems not specifically credited
ideas.where_published: La Longue Marche (1981) discusses the setting but not these matrix computations

ideas.what: Reduction of the ± ambiguity in the quotient by ±1 via g→−g, using ρ(−g)=−ρ(g).
ideas.modern_name: Lifting from PSL to SL / sign twist

missed.claim: Generic solutions require δ^3=1 in Z_ℓ. So nontrivial-determinant solutions of the linearized lacets equation exist only for ℓ≡1 mod 3: Z_3 contains no nontrivial cube roots of unity. The solution set's dependence on ℓ mod 3 is implicit here but not stated. It is a minor arithmetic observation, not a new result.
missed.quote: (84) δ^3 = 1 ... La nécessité de cette formule (84) était évidente a priori
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Marginal. It describes the shape of GT-type solutions in the linear quotient, a computation specialists would regard as routine.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine, correct matrix algebra solving the 3-cycle relation in PSL/PGL(2,Ẑ). Grothendieck himself labels the section 'par acquit de conscience, ne serviront peut-être plus'. Nothing here is a new result or connection.
transcription_corrections: In case 1, the Q formula should read Q = (c+d−a−b)/δ (= 1/δ^2 − a/δ), not 'Q = (c+d−bδ^2·b)/δ'.
The line 'ρρ(g) = +ρ^{-1}(g^{-1})' should read 'gρ(g) = +ρ^{-1}(g^{-1})' (equation (82)). Likewise '(82) ρρ(g)ρ^2(g)=+1' should read 'gρ(g)ρ^2(g)=+1'.
Margin: 'Quitte à remplacer g par −g, on se ramène à des solutions de l'équation (82)' — the replacement is plausibly g→−g, not 'δ(g)^{-1} g'.
Under (81), 'si det g=+1' refers to the alternative expression R=(c+d)(c+d−b)−δ.
